title: Simulated control-plane glitch: tiered circuit-breaker behavior & capacity reclamation rehearsal
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: validate system behavior when the control plane experiences a partial outage that causes stale routing decisions and delayed pool drain signals. This test focuses on three coordinated areas: (1) tiered circuit-breakers (global -> region -> tenant), (2) graceful capacity reclamation and GPU pool eviction flows, and (3) downstream dependency "blackhole" emulation that makes sidecars and proxies non-responsive. We want to ensure the platform preserves SLOs where possible, sheds load in a fair per-tenant manner, and recovers without producing latent correctness/regression issues (e.g., stuck KV caches, endless retry storms, or stale route pinning). This experiment differs from previous chaos tests by targeting control-plane metadata staleness rather than only forcing compute exhaustion or network partitions. Specific risks to validate: - Requests routed to drained hosts that still accept in-flight tokens and exhaust KV caches. - Circuit-breakers that trip too early or too late, causing unfair tenant starvation. - Admission-control decisions that do not reclaim memory/slots from dead processes. - Rollout/rollback logic when fallback model variants are used under pressure.
acceptance_criteria: When the control-plane glitch is injected, 99th percentile tail latency for critical customer routes remains below 1.8x baseline or automated traffic is shifted to fallback tiers without exceeding error budget
Tenant-level fairness: no single customer should see >3x increase in error-rate compared to their baseline while others remain stable (simulate multi-tenant mix)
Circuit-breaker metrics (tripped_count, recovery_time) are emitted and correlate with admission-control actions in traces/dashboards
No persistent KV cache divergence after recovery: KV cache hit-rate returns to >98% within 10 minutes and there are no orphaned large-cache allocations after pool recycling
Automated rollback and warmup: after capacity reclamation, new hosts accept traffic and pass healthchecks within defined warmup window (<=2m) without causing a retry storm
tasks: Design failure injection: implement control-plane delay of routing updates (configurable ms range and jitter) in chaos harness
Extend chaos harness to simultaneously emulate dependency blackhole (sidecar/proxy returns TCP RST or stalls) for a subset of aux services
Create tenant-mix traffic generator (small/medium/large) to exercise fairness policies under real request fanout
Instrument additional telemetry: emit tenant-scoped circuit-breaker counters, pool-eviction markers, prewarm/warmup events, and KV cache snapshot diffs
Run dry-run in staging with capture scripts, collect traces/dump artifacts (heap snapshots, kv-index snapshots), and hold postmortem review
If metrics pass, schedule progressively larger run in canary region followed by cross-region exercise
